context.title: Thrive LA voter guide — November 3, 2026 California general election endorsements

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure TE (Property Transfer Tax Exemption for Victims of January 2025 Fire Disaster)

positions.statement: Vote Yes on Measure TE. Fire victims deserve relief, not a transfer tax bill.

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure LA (City Infrastructure, Budget, Finance, and Contracting)

positions.statement: Vote No on Measure LA.

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure PL (City Planning Department)

positions.statement: The reforms Measure PL attempts are needed. The vehicle it uses is flawed.

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure EE (City Ethics, Elections, and Governance)

positions.statement: Voters should reject Measure EE and demand these proposals come back as separate, honest questions.

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure PRK (City Department of Recreation and Parks Budget)

positions.statement: Vote Yes on PRK. Los Angeles parks deserve a funding floor, and Los Angeles taxpayers deserve a city government that can prioritize.

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure PRT (City Airports, Harbor, and Water and Power Departments)

positions.statement: Vote Yes on Measure PRT.

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure FD (Funding for the Los Angeles Fire Department Through a One-Half Percent Sales Tax)

positions.statement: This is a trade-off, not a celebration.

subject.title: Los Angeles City — Measure SC (Los Angeles Unified School District Campaign Finance Rules Related to Board of Education Elections)

positions.statement: Measure SC costs taxpayers nothing, creates no new regulations or fees, and streamlines a clunky process. Vote yes.

subject.title: Los Angeles County Sheriff

positions.statement: Robert Luna has earned a second term through results, not rhetoric.

subject.title: Superior Court of Los Angeles County, Office 64

positions.statement: Maria Ghobadi is the proven, principled jurist Los Angeles needs on the Superior Court bench.

subject.title: Superior Court of Los Angeles County, Office 65

positions.statement: Anna Slotky Reitano has the courtroom depth and institutional knowledge to serve effectively on the Superior Court.

subject.title: Superior Court of Los Angeles County, Office 87

positions.statement: David DeJute is the experienced, no-nonsense judge Los Angeles County needs on the Superior Court.

subject.title: Superior Court of Los Angeles County, Office 131

positions.statement: Donna Tryfman is the experienced, balanced, public-safety-minded judge LA County's Superior Court needs.

subject.title: Los Angeles County — Measure A (Charter Amendment Reiterating Good Faith Negotiation Obligations and Establishing Impartial Binding Arbitration for Certified Public Safety Employee Disputes)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Measure A.

subject.title: Los Angeles County — Measure E (Ethics Commission and Community Investment Budget Allocation Charter Amendment)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Measure E.

subject.title: California Insurance Commissioner

positions.statement: Ben Allen is the experienced, substantive Insurance Commissioner California needs.

subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.statement: Thrive LA supports Proposition 1, but with clear eyes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: On balance, however, we support Proposition 2.

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.statement: Californians were promised a temporary tax, and Proposition 3 makes it permanent. Vote No on Proposition 3.

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: Proposition 4 is a reasonable, narrowly scoped reform that returns local control to local voters.

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.statement: Vote No on Proposition 5. The recall belongs to the voters, not the political establishment.

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: Proposition 37 is a reasonable, narrowly targeted tool to help working Californians buy homes. Vote yes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: Vote No on Proposition 38.

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: Vote YES on Proposition 39. Election integrity is not a partisan cause.

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: Vote No on Proposition 40. It is a wealth tax that will drive capital out of California, shrink the tax base, and establish a dangerous precedent for taxing savings at every income level.

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Proposition 41.

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: Vote Yes on Proposition 42. It is the most important taxpayer protection on the 2026 ballot.

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Proposition 43. It is the strongest taxpayer protection measure on this ballot.

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: Vote No on Proposition 44. It will close clinics, eliminate jobs, and reduce healthcare access for the Californians who need it most.

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Proposition 45. It is the most consequential pro-housing, pro-growth measure on the 2026 ballot.
